compiled_state.title: As a release engineer, I can run audit-closure-checks-migration.sh to identify all planning artifacts needing Closure Checks migration
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Story

As a release engineer preparing to migrate existing epics and stories to the `## Closure Checks` schema, I can run a single audit script to get a complete list of planning artifacts that lack the new section — so I know the migration scope before running the bulk migration.

## Done Definitions

- DD1: `plugins/dso/scripts/audit-closure-checks-migration.sh` created, executable (`chmod +x`), and tested; scans all tickets in `.tickets-tracker/` and reports which epics/stories lack a `## Closure Checks` section
- DD2: Script output format: one tab-separated line per ticket needing migration — `<ticket-id>\t<type>\t<status>\t<title>`; exits 0 (found tickets to migrate), 1 (all tickets already migrated), or 2 (error)
- DD3: All existing pointer references updated to post-migration locations — `← Satisfies:` annotations in preplanning SKILL.md Phase H that point to SC text which will move to `## Closure Checks` are updated to use the `← Validates Closure Check:` form (defined in S8)
- DD4: **CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table** updated with a `## Closure Checks` row — section name, what it contains (durable end-state intent, not transitional work), and which skill/step writes it

← Satisfies: "SC4: audit-closure-checks-migration.sh script created with correct output format"
← Satisfies: "SC5: pointer references updated to post-migration locations"
← Satisfies: "SC8: CLAUDE.md Quick Reference row added for ## Closure Checks"

## Considerations

- **CLAUDE.md Quick Reference must ship at S3 closure** — not deferred to S6. Stories S4, S5, S7, S8, S9, S10 all need the Quick Reference row to understand the `## Closure Checks` convention while implementing. Deferring to S6 creates a circular dependency.
- Audit script must handle large ticket collections gracefully — scan in batches if needed, with progress output for visibility.

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
